reading.rtitle: How to Eat at a Lokanta -- A Guide for Visitors
paras: A lokanta is a simple Turkish restaurant for workers and families. The food is ready, and you can see all the dishes behind a glass window. You do not need a menu: you point at the food you want, and the waiter brings it to your table.

Many dishes are stuffed or grilled. Dolma are peppers or grape leaves stuffed with rice, and they taste a little sour with lemon. Grilled meat and fish come with bread and salad. Most lokantas have a full portion and a half portion, and a half portion is enough for lunch.

To drink, many Turkish people order ayran, a cold yogurt drink. It tastes salty, not sweet. After lunch, try a small glass of Turkish tea. If you want dessert, baklava tastes very sweet, but remember that it has nuts. The price is usually low, and you pay at the front.

listenings.text: Welcome to our lokanta. This is how it works. You do not need a menu. Come to the front and look at the food behind the glass. You point at the dishes you want, and we bring them to your table. Today we have lentil soup. It tastes a little sour, because we serve it with lemon. We also have stuffed peppers with rice, and grilled chicken with salad. A half portion is cheaper, and it is a good size for lunch. To drink, try ayran. It is a cold yogurt drink, and it tastes salty. Please pay at the front when you finish. Enjoy your meal.

Hello, everybody, and welcome to my cooking class in Istanbul. I am Selin. Today we make two famous Turkish sweets. The first is baklava. It has thin pastry, butter, sugar and pistachio nuts, so it tastes very sweet. If you are allergic to nuts, please tell me now. The second is Turkish delight. It looks like small colorful cubes, and it smells of roses. At the end, we drink Turkish coffee together. It tastes strong and a little bitter, so many people drink it with a sweet. The class takes two hours, and you can take the sweets home in a box.

extra_audio.text: First, you walk into a small lokanta near the Grand Bazaar. Then you look at the dishes behind the glass, and the food looks delicious. Next, you point at the stuffed peppers and you ask for a half portion. After that, you try ayran, and it tastes salty. Finally, you finish with a small glass of tea and you pay at the front.
